scope: A defensible average-smoothness bound for the current factored CT objective on the feasible product of spectral balls; no new ProxSARAH or PALM variant has been selected or run.

references.relevance: Assumption 2.2, equation (4), page 9 requires average component-gradient smoothness. The constant L is not merely the smoothness of the averaged objective.
The CPU line_fanflat model uses nonnegative ray/pixel intersection lengths; the geometry bound below applies to that ideal linear model.

definitions.component: f_i(U,V)=||A_i(UV^T)-y_i||_2^2/(2d), with one component per view and d=956 detector bins.
definitions.objective: f=(1/N) sum_i f_i. A batch gradient in ct_problem.py divides by |B|d.
definitions.domain: K={(U,V): ||U||_op<=R_U, ||V||_op<=R_V, U>=0, V>=0}; factors have r=64 columns.
definitions.target_assumption: (1/N) sum_i ||grad f_i(x)-grad f_i(z)||^2 <= L^2 ||x-z||^2 for x,z in the domain queried by the method.

derivation: Let X=UV^T, H_i=A_i^* A_i/d and G_i=A_i^*(A_i X-y_i)/d. Let B_{U,V}(DeltaU,DeltaV)=DeltaU V^T+U DeltaV^T.
The joint Hessian is B^* H_i B plus the self-adjoint residual cross operator (DeltaU,DeltaV)->(G_i DeltaV,G_i^T DeltaU).
||UV^T||_F<=sqrt(r) R_U R_V, hence ||G_i||_op<=q_i sqrt(r) R_U R_V+sqrt(q_i) s_i.
Therefore L_i=q_i (R_U^2+R_V^2+sqrt(r) R_U R_V)+sqrt(q_i) s_i bounds the joint Hessian norm uniformly on the product spectral balls.
The domain is convex; integration along its line segments gives component-gradient Lipschitz constants L_i on this domain.
L=sqrt((1/N)sum_i L_i^2) therefore satisfies the average-smoothness inequality on the domain.
If q_i<=qbar uniformly, Minkowski gives the simpler valid bound L=qbar (R_U^2+R_V^2+sqrt(r) R_U R_V)+sqrt(qbar) ||y_train||_2/sqrt(Nd).

why_initial_block_sum_is_not_joint_L.scalar_counterexample: f(u,v)=0.5(uv)^2 at u=v=1 has block curvatures 1 and 1, but joint Hessian [[1,2],[2,1]] has spectral norm 3>2.
why_initial_block_sum_is_not_joint_L.additional_current_implementation_issues: The saved L_U^0 and L_V^0 come from ten power iterations on only 120 calibration views and the initial opposite-factor spectral norms. The spectral caps are twice the initial factor spectral norms, and cross/residual Hessian terms are absent. Neither the current joint Hessian nor the component-average smoothness condition is certified by their sum.

assumptions: Square grid of side w and pixel width h=w/512.
Source rotates at distance S from the origin; the flat detector is D behind the origin with uniform spacing delta.
The shifted volume lies in the disk of radius rho=w/sqrt(2)+||volume_center||<S.
The exact forward matrix consists of nonnegative zero-thickness intersection lengths.
derivation: In coordinates aligned with the source, the detector coordinate of a point is t(x,y)=(S+D)y/(S-x).
On the containing disk, ||grad t||_2 <= G=(S+D)/(S-rho) sqrt(1+(rho/(S-rho))^2).
A pixel has diameter sqrt(2)h, so its detector shadow has length at most sqrt(2)h G. At most m=floor(sqrt(2)h G/delta)+1 ray centers can lie in this interval.
Every row sum of A_i is at most sqrt(2)w. Every column sum is at most m sqrt(2)h.

illustration.data_read: One cached sinogram, cast to float32 exactly as CTProblem does; only scalar measurement statistics were calculated. No projector, optimizer or benchmark was run.

limitations_and_applicability: This is an analytic bound for the stated exact linear ray-weight model. It is not an interval-arithmetic certificate for ASTRA FP32 projector geometry, stored weights or accumulation.
The factored objective is quartic and is not globally smooth on all unconstrained factor space. The stated bound holds on the convex product spectral balls, including its nonnegative subset.

Applying the paper proof with this restricted-domain bound requires verifying that all gradient query points and descent line segments stay in that domain. Projection onto K and relaxation weights in [0,1] have this property; it should be stated rather than claiming unconstrained global smoothness.
The bound is conservative. It does not establish that the true average-smoothness constant is approximately 33 or that a smaller empirical constant is invalid.

A finite power-iteration estimate is not an upper bound. No author-supported backtracking replacement or iterate-dependent L rule was established in this audit. The paper adaptive scheme computes its relaxation schedule from a fixed L; it does not make local-curvature adaptation automatic.
No new variant, smoothness constant or parameter setting is adopted by this note. Choosing between published ProxSARAH variants requires a separate explicit implementation decision.
